Merge simplification can hide side-branch commits, but stage-1 has 0 merges. Run: `git log --oneline stage-1 -- .env | wc -l` -> 0; `git log --all --full-history --oneline -- .env | wc -l` -> 0.

Code inspection at stage-1: Program.cs l.23-39 validates tokens with `new SymmetricSecurityKey(Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(signingKey))` from `Jwt:SigningKey`; ValidIssuer/ValidAudience come from committed appsettings.json (`donhang-api`/`donhang-app`), so the key is the only non-public input — holder can sign a token with any `sub`. Connection string uses Username=donhang with the password to reach the donhang database.

Security practice, not a documented behaviour of a pinned version. Nearest official text found: Docker docs best-practices "Be cautious about including sensitive data in environment variables." The mechanism the lesson uses to justify it (Git keeps committed versions) is verified under claim 4. No doc in versions.yaml roots states "replace when leaked"; kind is opinion so not blocking.

issues.text: Definition of untracked is inaccurate. Untracked means not in the index (not in the next commit), not "never told". A file deleted in a commit (quiz q2) or removed with `git rm --cached` was once included in commits but is untracked afterwards, and .gitignore does apply to it. With the lesson's wording a learner concludes the opposite.
issues.quote: files Git has never been told to include in commits
issues.fix: Replace with: "files that would not be part of your next commit unless you `git add` them".

issues.text: Compose does not write values into the file; it substitutes them in the model it builds when reading the file. "fills its values into docker-compose.yml" can read as editing the committed file, which section 5 then says stays a template.
issues.quote: Compose reads it and fills its values into `docker-compose.yml`
issues.fix: Replace with: "Compose reads it and fills its values into the `${...}` placeholders of `docker-compose.yml` as it reads that file (the file itself is not changed)".

issues.text: Claims 1, 4 and 5 are Git behaviour (git add ignore rule, gitignore on tracked files, git log path filtering) but carry no version_key; versions.yaml pins `git` 2.46.
issues.quote: ignored untracked paths are not picked up by git add (without --force)

issues.text: The new untracked explanation is inserted as an appositive in the middle of the sentence, so the sentence has three commas-separated parts and I read it twice to find the main verb ("that Git should ignore"). The meaning is now clear once untangled.
issues.quote: a file listing untracked paths, files that would not be part of your next commit unless you `git add` them, that Git should ignore, so `git add` does not pick them up by accident.
issues.fix: Split into two sentences: "`.gitignore` — a file listing untracked paths Git should ignore, so `git add` does not pick them up by accident. Untracked files are ones that would not be part of your next commit unless you `git add` them."

issues.text: Three references to files in one clause: "reads it", "as it reads that file", "without changing the file". I had to re-read to be sure "it" is .env and "that file"/"the file" is docker-compose.yml.
issues.quote: Compose reads it and fills its values into the `${...}` placeholders of `docker-compose.yml` as it reads that file, without changing the file
issues.fix: Name the files: "Compose reads `.env` and, while reading `docker-compose.yml`, fills those values into its `${...}` placeholders without changing `docker-compose.yml` itself".
